en: One fascicle of the *Rucirakūṭa-dhāraṇī-sūtra*, compiled by the Śramaṇa Zhisheng of Chongfu Monastery during the Tang Dynasty; translated by the Tripitaka Master Bodhiruci of India during the Tang Dynasty.

*The Mañjuśrī-mūla-ekākṣara-dhāraṇī-sūtra*, one fascicle; translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Prajñādeva of the Tang Dynasty. *The Mañjuśrī-bodhisattva-mantra-piṭaka-ekākṣara-mantra-rāja-sūtra*, one fascicle;

translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Yijing during the reign of Empress Wu of the Tang Dynasty. *The Twelve Buddha-nāma-divya-mantra-sūtra*, one fascicle; translated by the Indian Tripiṭaka Master Jñānagupta and others of the Sui Dynasty.
*The Tathāgata-guṇa-varṇana-divya-mantra-sūtra*, one fascicle; translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Yijing of the Tang Dynasty. *The Avalokiteśvara-bodhisattva-cintāmaṇi...* [text fragment]

*The Dhāraṇī Sūtra*, one fascicle; translated by Tripiṭaka Master Yijing of the Tang dynasty. *The Mahāmāyūrī-vidyārājñī Sūtra*, one fascicle; translated by Tripiṭaka Master Kumārajīva of the Yao Qin dynasty.

*The Mahāsuvarṇa-mahāmāyūrī-vidyārājñī Sūtra*, one fascicle; translator lost. *The Buddha-bhāṣita Mahāsuvarṇa-mahāmāyūrī-vidyārājñī Sūtra*, one fascicle; translator lost. *The Mahāmāyūrī-vidyārājñī Sūtra*, two fascicles;

seventh translation by Tripiṭaka Master Saṃghavarman of Funan during the Liang dynasty. *The Mahāmāyūrī Sūtra*, three fascicles; translated by Tripiṭaka Master Yijing at the Inner Monastery in the Eastern Capital (Luoyang) during the Tang dynasty.
The eleven sūtras translated by Fǎchăng, totaling fourteen fascicles in one volume, comprise one hundred seventy-one sheets.

The *Dhāraṇī-saṃgraha-sūtra*, twelve fascicles, translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Ādigupta of Central India during the Tang Dynasty. The *Ekādaśamukha-avalokiteśvara-mantra-sūtra*, one fascicle, translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Yaśogupta of India and others during the Northern Zhou dynasty of the Yuwen clan.
The *Ekādaśamukha-mantra-hṛdaya-sūtra*, one fascicle, translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Xuanzang of the Tang Dynasty. The *Mahā...* [text truncated]

*Li-zhi-tian-jing* (Sūtra on the Goddess Īśvarī), one fascicle; translator lost. *Zhou-wu-shou-jing* (Sūtra of Five Dhāraṇīs), one fascicle; translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Xuanzang of the Tang. *Qian-zhuan-tuo-luo-ni-guan-shi-yin-puti-sa-zhou-jing* (Sūtra of the Thousand-Turn Dhāraṇī and the Mantra of Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva), one fascicle;

translated by the Śramaṇa Zhìtōng of Tóngzhí Temple during the Tang. *Liu-zi-shen-zhou-jing* (Sūtra of the Six-Syllable Divine Dhāraṇī), one fascicle; translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Bodhiruci of Central India during the Tang.

*Qi-juzhi-fo-da-xin-zhunti-tuo-luo-ni-jing* (Sūtra of the Great-Mind Cundī Dhāraṇī of Seven Koṭis of Buddhas), one fascicle; translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Divākara of Central India during the Tang. *Qi-juzhi-fo-mu* (The Mother of Seven Koṭis of Buddhas).

The *Cundā-mahāvidyā-dhāraṇī-sūtra*, one fascicle, translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Vajrabodhi of the Tang Dynasty. [Total for] the nine preceding sūtras: twenty fascicles in two volumes, totaling three hundred and eighty-nine sheets.

The *Avalokiteśvara-bodhisattva-svacitta-mantra-sūtra*, one fascicle, translated by the Śramaṇa Zhìtōng of Zǒngchí Monastery during the Tang Dynasty. The *Sūtra of Various Miscellaneous Dhāraṇīs*, one fascicle, [translated during the] Northern Zhou dynasty of the Yùwén clan.

*The Sūtra of the Supreme Dhāraṇī of the Buddha’s Uṣṇīṣa*, translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Śikṣānanda of India; *The Sūtra of the Most Victorious Dhāraṇī of the Buddha’s Uṣṇīṣa*, translated by Du Xingyi, Court Gentleman of the Tang Dynasty, by Imperial Decree;

*The Sūtra of the Uṣṇīṣavijayā Dhāraṇī*, translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Divākara of Central India during the Tang Dynasty; *The Sūtra of the Most Victorious Uṣṇīṣa Dhāraṇī for Purifying Karmic Obstructions*, translated by the Śramaṇa Buddhapālita of Kaśmīr during the Tang Dynasty;
[The Sūtra of the Most Victorious Uṣṇīṣa Dhāraṇī for Purifying Karmic Obstructions], translated by the Tripiṭaka Master [of] Central India during the Tang Dynasty.

*The Sūtra of the Buddha-Uṣṇīṣa-Vijaya-Dhāraṇī*, one fascicle, translated twice in the Eastern Capital by Divākara; *The Sūtra of the Dhāraṇī of the Immeasurable Gate of Subtle Secrets*, one fascicle, translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Yi Jing of the Tang;

*The Sūtra of the Emergence of the Immeasurable Gate Dhāraṇī*, one fascicle, translated by the Upāsaka Zhi Qian of the Wu, a Yuezhi person; *The Sūtra of the Immeasurable Gate Dhāraṇī*, one fascicle, translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Buddhabhadra of India during the Eastern Jin;
*The Ānandamukha-nirhāra-dhāraṇī Sūtra*, one fascicle, translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Guṇabhadra of India during the Song; and the *Sūtra of the Immeasurable Gate*.
*The Dhāraṇī Sūtra for the Destruction of Māra*, one fascicle; translated by the Western Region śramaṇa Guṇabhadra and Xuanchang during the Song dynasty.

*The Ānandamukha-hārī-dhāraṇī Sūtra*, one fascicle; translated by the Indian Tripiṭaka Master Buddhasanta during the Northern Wei dynasty. *The Śāriputra-dhāraṇī Sūtra*, one fascicle; translated by the Funan Tripiṭaka Master Saṃghavarman during the Liang dynasty.
*The Ekottarābhinirhāra-bodhisattva Sūtra*, one fascicle; translated by the Indian Tripiṭaka Master Jñānagupta and others during the Sui dynasty. *The Anantamukha-nirhāra-dhāraṇī*.

*Ni jing* (Nun Sūtra), one fascicle; translated by the Śramaṇa Zhìyán of Zhìxiāng Monastery during the Táng dynasty. *Shèngchāng bìyìn tuóluóní jīng* (Sūtra of the Dhāraṇī of the Victorious Banner Arm Seal), one fascicle; translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Xuánzàng of the Táng dynasty.

*Miàobì yīnzhāng tuóluóní jīng* (Sūtra of the Dhāraṇī of the Wondrous Arm Seal Banner), one fascicle; translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Śikṣānanda of Khotan during the Táng dynasty. These seventeen sūtras, totaling seventeen fascicles, are contained in the same volume and comprise one hundred and sixty-one pages.

*The Scripture on the Dharma-Gate of Holding the Limitless Abyss*, one fascicle; translated by the Qifu Qin śramaṇa Śrīghana. *The Scripture on the Dhāraṇī of All Dharmas Entering the Gate of the Immeasurable as Asked by the Bodhisattva Uṣṇīṣavijayā*, one fascicle;
translated by the Gao Qi layman Wan Tianyi. *The Scripture on the Vajra-Supreme-Taste Dhāraṇī*, one fascicle; translated by the Indian Tripiṭaka Master Buddhasanta of the Northern Wei.
*The Scripture on the Vajramaṇḍala Dhāraṇī*, one fascicle; translated by the Indian Tripiṭaka Master Jñānagupta and others of the Sui. *The Lion’s Valiant Dash*.

*The Sūtra of the Questions of the Bodhisattva*, one fascicle; translator lost. *The Dhāraṇī Sūtra of the Flower Cluster*, one fascicle; translator lost. *The Divine Dhāraṇī Sūtra of the Flower Accumulation*, one fascicle;

translated by the Wu-period Yuezhi layman Zhi Qian. *The Sūtra of the Six-Syllable King of Mantras*, one fascicle. *The Sūtra of the Six-Syllable Divine King of Mantras*, one fascicle. *The Sūtra of the Seven Buddhas Asked by the Bodhisattva Ākāśagarbha*, one fascicle.

These three sūtras are all of lost translation. *The Sūtra of the Tathāgata’s Skillful Means and Secret Mantras*, one fascicle; translated by the Sui-period Indian Tripiṭaka Master Jñānagupta and others.

*Yi-chi-ju-shen-chou ching* (Sūtra on the Dhāraṇī-mantra of Holding the Words), one fascicle; translated by the Wu-period Yuezhi upāsaka Zhi Qian. *Duo-lin-ni-po ching* (Dhāraṇī-pātra Sūtra), one fascicle; translated by the Eastern Jin-period Western Region śramaṇa Zhu Tanwulan.
*Dong-fang-zui-sheng-deng-wang-rulai ching* (Sūtra of the Tathāgata Supreme Lamp King of the East), one fascicle; translated by the Sui-period Indian Tripiṭaka Master Jñānagupta and others.

*Shan-fa-fangbian-tuoloni-zhou ching* (Sūtra of the Dhāraṇī-mantra of Skillful Means of Good Dharma), one fascicle; translator lost. *Jingang-mimi-shanmen-tuoloni ching* (Vajra Secret Gate of Goodness Dhāraṇī Sūtra), one fascicle; translator lost. *Hu-ming-famen-shenzhou* (Divine Mantra of the Life-Protecting Dharma-Gate).

*Sūtra*, one fascicle; translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Bodhiruci of India during the Tang Dynasty. *Amoghapāśa-vimala-prabhāsa-mahādhāraṇī-sūtra*, one fascicle; translated by the Śramaṇa Mito-shan from the Western Regions during the Tang Dynasty.

*Sūtra on the Dhāraṇī Mantra for Invoking Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva to Eliminate and Subdue Poisonous Harm*, one fascicle; translated by the Layman Zhu Nanti of Foreign Lands during the Eastern Jin Dynasty.
These sixteen sūtras, totaling nineteen fascicles, are contained in the same volume, comprising one hundred and sixty-seven sheets.
*The Scripture on the Inner Treasury of a Hundred Jewels*, one fascicle; translated by the Yuezhi Tripiṭaka Master Zhīlújiāchèn of the Later Han.

*The Scripture on Bathing the Assembly of Monks in the Warm Chamber*, one fascicle; translated by the Anxi Tripiṭaka Master Ān Shìgāo of the Later Han. *The Sūrala-sūtra*, one fascicle; translated by the Yuezhi Upāsaka Zhīshīlún of the Former Liáng.

*The Sūrala-sūtra*, one fascicle; translated by the Western Region Tripiṭaka Master Bóyán of the Cáo Wèi. *The Sihe Samādhi Sūtra*, one fascicle; translated by the Yuezhi Upāsaka Zhīqián of the Wù. *The Scripture on the Birthplace of the Bodhisattva*, one fascicle.

*The Sutra on the Four Unobtainables*, one fascicle, translated by Zhi Qian. *The Sutra on the Brahma Maiden’s Guarding of the Mind*, one fascicle, translated by the Tripitaka Master Dharmarakṣa of the Western Jin.

*The Sutra on the Samādhi of Perfect Radiance*, one fascicle, translated by the Tripitaka Master Zhi Yao of the Western Regions during the Later Han. *The Sutra on the Jewel Net*, one fascicle, translated by the Tripitaka Master Dharmarakṣa of the Western Jin.

*The Sutra on the Bodhisattva’s Practice of the Fifty Physical Conditions*, one fascicle, translated by the Tripitaka Master Dharmarakṣa of the Western Jin. *The Sutra on the Bodhisattva’s Cultivation of Practice*, one fascicle, translated by the Tripitaka Master Dharmarakṣa of the Western Jin. ... [and so forth] ... West.

*Zhude fudian jing* (Sūtra on the Fields of Merit for the Virtuous), one fascicle, translated by the Śramaṇa Bai Fazhu of Henei during the Jin dynasty. *Dafangdeng rulai zang jing* (Mahāvaipulya Tathāgatagarbha Sūtra), one fascicle, translated jointly by the Śramaṇas Fali and Faju of the Western Jin dynasty.

*Foyu jing* (Sūtra of the Buddha’s Words), one fascicle, translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Buddhabhadra of India during the Eastern Jin dynasty. *Jinsewang jing* (Sūtra of King Suvarṇavarṇa), one fascicle, translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Bodhiruci of India during the Northern Wei dynasty.

*Yandao suye jing* (Sūtra on the Exposition of the Deeds of the Laity and Monastics), one fascicle, translated by the Brahmin Gautama Prajñāruci of India during the Northern Wei dynasty. [The text continues: ...of the Qifu...

*The Sutra of the Names of One Hundred Buddhas*, translated by the Qin śramaṇa Shengjian, one fascicle; and the eighteen sutras translated by the Sui Tripiṭaka Master Narendrayaśas, eighteen fascicles;
together in one volume, totaling one hundred and fifty-six sheets.

*The Sūtra on Praising the Merits of All Buddhas*, three fascicles; translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Kiṅkiaya of the Western Regions together with Tanyao during the Northern Wei. *The Sūtra of the Devaputra Susīma*, two fascicles; translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Dharmarakṣa of the Western Jin. *The Mahāmāyā Sūtra*, two fascicles; translated by the Śramaṇa Shi Tanying of the Xiao Qi. *The Sūtra on Eliminating Fear and Calamities*, one fascicle; translated by the Śramaṇa Shengjian of the Qifu Qin. *The Pai Sūtra*, one fascicle; translated by the Upāsaka Zhi Qian of Yuezhi during the Wu. *The Sūtra on the Prediction of Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva*, one fascicle; translated by the Śramaṇa Shi Tanwujie of Huanglong during the Song. These six sūtras comprise ten fascicles in a single volume, totaling one hundred and eighty-six sheets. [Revised].

The *Sāgaranāgarājaparipṛcchā-sūtra*, four fascicles; translated by the Tripitaka Master Zhu Fahu of the Western Jin. The *Śūraṅgamasamādhi-sūtra*, three fascicles; translated by the Tripitaka Master Kumārajīva of the Yao Qin. The *Bhadracarīpraṇidhāna-sūtra*, one fascicle; translated by the Tripitaka Master Dharmamitra of Kaśmīr during the Song dynasty. The *Bhaiṣajyarāja-bhaiṣajyasamudgata-sūtra*, one fascicle; translated by the Tripitaka Master Jñānayaśas from the Western Regions during the Song dynasty. The *Acintyaprabhāsa-bodhisattvaparipṛcchā-sūtra*, one fascicle; translated by the Tripitaka Master Kumārajīva of the Yao Qin. These five sūtras comprise ten fascicles in a single volume, totaling one hundred and seventy-seven pages. [De].

*The Scripture on the Ten Abodes and the Severing of Bonds*, fourteen fascicles, translated by the Śramaṇa Zhu Fonian of Liangzhou during the Yao Qin dynasty. *The Scripture on the Essential Collection of All Buddhas*, two fascicles, translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Zhu Fahu of the Western Jin dynasty. *The Scripture on Unprecedented Causes and Conditions*, two fascicles, translated by the Śramaṇa Shi Tanjing of the Xiao Qi dynasty. These three scriptures comprise eighteen fascicles in two volumes, totaling two hundred seventy-two sheets. [Neng] [Mo].

The *Bodhisattva-alaṃkāra-sūtra* in thirteen fascicles, translated by the Śramaṇa Zhu Fonian of Liangzhou during the Yao Qin dynasty; and the *Cārudin-samādhi-sūtra* in two fascicles, translated by the lay believer Nie Chengyuan of the Western Jin dynasty. These two scriptures comprise fifteen fascicles in two volumes, totaling two hundred and ninety-four sheets. [Characters: 忘 (wàng) and 罔 (wǎng)].

The *Bhadra-kalpika-sūtra*, ten fascicles, translated by the Tripitaka Master Dharmarakṣa of the Western Jin; from one bundle, totaling two hundred and one sheets (the Southern Canon records it as two hundred and one sheets). [Discussion].

Mahāyāna Sūtras Translated Individually: One Hundred and Thirty Works in Two Hundred and Ninety-Three Fascicles, Arranged in Twenty Sets. *Mahādharmapradīpa-dhāraṇī-sūtra*, twenty fascicles, translated by the Sui Dynasty Indian Tripiṭaka Master Jñānagupta and others. From the second set, totaling three hundred and sixty sheets. [That] [Short].

The Mahātejas-dhāraṇī-sūtra, twenty fascicles, translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Jñānagupta of India during the Sui Dynasty; comprising two bundles, totaling two hundred and seventy-four sheets. [Characters: 靡 (mǐ) and 恃 (shì)].

*Foming jing* (Sūtra on the Names of Buddhas), twelve fascicles; translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Bodhiruci of India during the Northern Wei dynasty. *Sanjie sanqian foming jing* (Sūtra on the Names of Three Thousand Buddhas of the Three Kalpas), three fascicles. *Guozhuangyanjie qianfoming jing* (Sūtra on the Names of One Thousand Buddhas of the Past Adornment Kalpa), one fascicle. *Xianjie qianfoming jing* (Sūtra on the Names of One Thousand Buddhas of the Present Auspicious Kalpa), one fascicle. *Weilai xingsujie qianfoming jing* (Sūtra on the Names of One Thousand Buddhas of the Future Constellation Kalpa), one fascicle. [Translator lost]; recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*. The above two works comprise two bundles and fifteen fascicles, totaling 367 sheets. [Ji] [Cháng].

*The Sutra of the Names of Five Thousand Five Hundred Buddhas*, eight fascicles; translated by Jñānagupta and others of India during the Sui dynasty. *The Sutra on the Inconceivable Merits and the Protection and Mindfulness of All Buddhas*, two fascicles; translated during the Cao Wei period, the name of the Tripiṭaka Master lost. These two sutras comprise ten fascicles in one volume, totaling one hundred and sixty-six pages. 【Xin】.

The *Puṣpamālā-sūtra* (Flower-Hand Sūtra), ten fascicles; also known as the *Sarvakuśalamūla-saṃgraha-sūtra* (Sūtra on Gathering All Roots of Virtue). Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Kumārajīva of the Yao Qin dynasty. This single case of ten fascicles comprises two hundred and thirty-six sheets. [Shǐ].

The Mahāvaipulya Dhāraṇī Sūtra, four fascicles; translated by the Śramaṇa Fa-zhong of the Northern Liang dynasty at Gaochang Commandery. The Saṃghāṭa Sūtra, four fascicles; translated by Prince Yueposhouna of Ujjayinī during the Northern Wei dynasty. The Balālaṃkāra Samādhi Sūtra, three fascicles; translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Narendrayaśas of India during the Sui dynasty. The Mahāvaipulya Tathāgatagarbha Bodhimaṇḍala-vyūha Sūtra (The Sūtra on the Perfect Enlightenment of the Great Extensive Meaning), one fascicle; translated by the Śramaṇa Buddhatoṭara of Kaśmīra during the Tang dynasty. These four sūtras comprise twelve fascicles in a single volume, totaling one hundred eighty-one pages. [Ke].

The *Buddhanusmṛtisamādhisāgara-sūtra* in ten fascicles, translated by the Tripitaka Master Buddhabhadra of India during the Eastern Jin dynasty; comprising one bundle, totaling one hundred and sixty-seven sheets. [Seal].

*Mahā-upāya-buddha-pratyupakāra-sūtra*, seven fascicles; translator lost. *Bodhisattva-pūrva-caryā-sūtra*, three fascicles; translator lost. These two preceding sūtras comprise ten fascicles in one volume, totaling one hundred eighty-one pages. [Vessel].

*The Scripture on the Collection of Dharmas*, six fascicles, translated by the Indian Tripiṭaka Master Bodhiruci of the Northern Wei; *The Scripture on the Contemplation of the Practice of All Dharmas*, four fascicles, translated by the Indian Tripiṭaka Master Jñānagupta and others of the Sui dynasty. These two scriptures comprise ten fascicles in one volume, totaling one hundred and ninety-five sheets. [Section: Desire].

The *Bodhisattva-utkṣepa-garbha-sūtra* in five fascicles, translated by the Śramaṇa Zhu Fonian of Liangzhou during the Yao Qin dynasty; the *Hongdao guangxian sanmei jing* in four fascicles, translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Zhu Fahu of the Western Jin; and the *Rendeng gongde jing* in one fascicle, translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Narendrayaśas of India during the Northern Qi. These three sūtras comprise ten fascicles in a single volume, totaling one hundred and ninety-one sheets. [Nan].

The *Aṅgulimālīya Sūtra* in four fascicles, translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Guṇabhadra of India during the Song dynasty; the *Sarvābhavabodhisattva Sūtra* in four fascicles, translated by the Tripiṭaka Masters Jñānagupta and others of India during the Sui dynasty; and the *Mahāprajñāpāramitā-śatapañcāśatikā-parīkṣā Sūtra* in two fascicles, translated by the Tripiṭaka Master An Shigao of Parthia during the Later Han dynasty. These three sūtras comprise ten fascicles in one volume, totaling one hundred eighty-three sheets. [Measurement].

*Zhongyin jing* (Sūtra on the Intermediate State), two fascicles, translated by the Śramaṇa Zhu Fonian of Liangzhou during the Yao Qin dynasty; *Dafagujing* (The Great Dharma Drum Sūtra), two fascicles, translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Guṇabhadra of India during the Song dynasty; *Wenshushili wenjing* (Sūtra of Mañjuśrī’s Questions), two fascicles, translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Saṃghanāla of Funan during the Liang dynasty; *Yue Shangnü Jing* (Sūtra of the Girl Candrottarā), two fascicles, translated by Jñānagupta and others of India during the Sui dynasty; *Dafangguang Rulai Mijizang Jing* (The Vaipulya Tathāgata-Guhyagarbha Sūtra), two fascicles, translator lost. These five sūtras comprise ten fascicles in one volume, totaling one hundred and ninety-four sheets. [Ink].

*Mahāyāna-Guhyakapūraṇa-sūtra*, three fascicles; translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Śīlabhadra of Central India during the Tang Dynasty. *Sūtra on Examining the Retribution of Good and Evil Karma*, two fascicles; translated by the foreign śramaṇa Bodhimitra. *Sūtra of the Lotus Face*, two fascicles; translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Narendrayaśas of India during the Sui Dynasty. *Sūtra of Mañjuśrī’s Questions on the Bodhisattva Stations*, one fascicle; translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Lokakṣema of the Yuezhi during the Later Han Dynasty. *Sūtra on the Merit of Casting Images of the Mahāyāna*, two fascicles; translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Ti-p’yun-po-lo of Khotan during the Tang Dynasty. The above five sūtras comprise ten fascicles in a single volume, totaling one hundred fifty-four pages. [Bi].

*The Great and Vast Jewel-Pavilion Well-Abiding Secret Dhāraṇī Sūtra*, three fascicles, translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Bodhiruci of South India during the Tang dynasty; *The One-Syllable Buddha-Uṣṇīṣa Cakravartin King Sūtra*, five fascicles, translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Bodhiruci of the Tang dynasty; *The Great Dhāraṇī One-Syllable Heart-Mantra Sūtra for the Age of Dharma-Deterioration*, one fascicle, translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Śubhakarasiṃha of North India during the Tang dynasty. These three sūtras comprise nine fascicles in a single volume, totaling one hundred and eighty-eight sheets. [Thread].

The *Śūraṅgama Sūtra*, in ten fascicles, concerning the Great Buddha-Crown Tathāgata’s Secret Cause, the Cultivation and Realization of the Definitive Meaning, and the Myriad Practices of All Bodhisattvas; translated by the Śramaṇa Huaidi of Xunzhou together with Indian monks at Guangzhou during the Tang Dynasty, comprising one bundle totaling one hundred and fifty-seven sheets. [Dye] (Ran).

*The Mahāvairocana-buddhotpatti-adhiṣṭhāna-vikurvita-sūtra*, seven fascicles, translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Śubhakarasiṃha of Central India during the Tang Dynasty, together with the Śramaṇa Yi Xing; *The Subāhu-paripṛcchā-sūtra*, three fascicles, translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Śubhakarasiṃha of India during the Tang Dynasty. These two sūtras comprise ten fascicles in one volume, totaling one hundred and sixty-three pages. [Poem].

*Susiddhikara Sūtra*, three fascicles; translated by the Tripitaka Master Śubhakarasiṃha of Central India during the Tang Dynasty. *Mūlamudrā-mantra-sūtra*, one fascicle; translator lost. *Ritual Manual for Recitation Briefly Extracted from the Vajraśekhara Yoga*, four fascicles; translated by the Tripitaka Master Vajrabodhi of South India during the Tang Dynasty. These three scriptures comprise eight fascicles in a single volume, totaling one hundred and eighty-six pages. [Praise].

*The Scripture on the Divine Incantations Spoken by the Seven Buddhas*, four fascicles; translated during the Jin Dynasty, the name of the Tripiṭaka Master lost; now appended to the Eastern Jin Catalogue.

*The Scripture on the Great Auspicious and Righteous Divine Incantations*, four fascicles; translated by the Śramaṇa Tanyao, Director of the Office of Monastic Affairs (Zhaoxuantong) under the Northern Wei.
*The Mañjuśrī-ratnakara-dhāraṇī Sūtra*, one fascicle; translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Bodhiruci of South India during the Tang Dynasty.
*The Dhāraṇī Sūtra of the Vajra Radiance for Stopping Wind and Rain*, one fascicle, translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Bodhiruci of the Tang Dynasty;
*The Dhāraṇī Sūtra of the Great General of Ghosts and Spirits Aṭavaka for Ascending to the Buddha*, one fascicle, translator lost;
*The Dhāraṇī Sūtra of King Amitābha’s Drum Sound*, one fascicle, translator lost; *The Great Samantabhadra Dhāraṇī*, [one fascicle], translator lost.
*Āṭānāṭīya Sūtra*, one fascicle; translator lost. *Mahāsaptaratna Dhāraṇī Sūtra*, one fascicle; translator lost. *Ṣaḍakṣara Mahādhāraṇī Sūtra*, one fascicle; translator lost.
*Anzhai Shenzhou Jing* (Sūtra on the Spirit-Spell for Dwelling Peace), one fascicle; translator lost during the Later Han.
The above six sūtras are contained in the same volume.
